title: Two pools, one of them saturated
request:
a pool per dependency, and a third call to the one that is already full

./your_program.sh bulkhead
init {"a":2,"b":2}
call a x1 0
call a x2 0
call a x3 0
call b y1 0
stats
note: The rejection is the feature. Queueing x3 instead would hold a caller, a connection and a timeout's worth of latency on a dependency that has already shown it cannot keep up, and it is the queue — not the slow dependency — that eventually takes the whole service down.

title: The same traffic with no bulkhead
request:
the identical four calls against one pool shared by both dependencies

./your_program.sh bulkhead
init-shared 2
call shared x1 0
call shared x2 0
call shared y1 0
stats
note: Nothing here is broken and nothing is misconfigured. One dependency simply got there first, and the caller that is refused is the one that would have succeeded. This is the failure the whole pattern exists to prevent.
